- Materials: Vocabulary cards, audio for the listening, reading handout, COSYmanuals A1 grammar pages for how old are you?, possessive adjectives.
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.

Core Active Vocabulary (5 items):

age — how old a person is. Example: My age is eighteen.
year — a period of twelve months. Example: I am twenty years old.
birthday — the day you were born. Example: My birthday is in May.
month — one of the twelve parts of a year. Example: June is a summer month.
January — the first month of the year. Example: January is cold here.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• How old are you?
• I am ... years old.
• When is your birthday?
• My birthday is in ...
• Her birthday is in May.
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'how old a person is'?
Which word means 'a period of twelve months'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Years old is stressed on old.
I am twenty years OLD.
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word has the target sound?
Mark the stressed syllable.
Grammar focus: How old are you?, possessive adjectives.
Ask How old are you? Answer I am twenty years old. Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, our, their. Example: Her birthday is in May.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Complete: ___ old are you?
Choose the correct possessive.
Complete the sentence.
Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
Anna is twenty years old. Her birthday is in January. Her brother is twelve years old.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: How old are you? B: I am nineteen years old. A: When is your birthday? B: In January.
Speaking: Asking age and birthday month in class survey

• How old are you?
• I am ... years old.
• When is your birthday?
Writing: Write 5 sentences about ages of family members
